fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the area between the main residence and the detached structure clear of parked vehicles and equipment to allow responders to move between buildings.
• Trim vegetation along the walkway so responders can move quickly between structures without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and work around all four sides.
• Post the solar panel system shutoff location and controls in a visible spot near the main electrical panel or primary entry point so arriving responders can locate it quickly.
• Mark the solar panel shutoff with a weatherproof label or sign readable at arm's length.
• Keep a clear path from the parking area to both structures free of stored materials, equipment, and overgrown plants.
• Create or maintain a spot in the parking area large enough for at least one emergency vehicle to turn around without backing onto the road.
• If the detached structure has a lockable door, keep a key accessible to responders or install a lockbox at the main residence entry.
• Cut back any dense vegetation that narrows or obscures the single driveway access point so approaching vehicles have a clear line of sight onto the property.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim lower branches on large trees near structures to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Thin the tree cluster to create open gaps between individual trees and reduce the amount of connected vegetation close to structures.
• Remove any dead wood, dry leaves, or fallen branches from beneath scattered trees near the house.
• Clear shrubs and low plants that grow directly against or touching any side of the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath large trees near the house free of accumulated dead plant material.
• Separate any shrubs or small plants growing beneath tree canopies to reduce the connection between ground-level vegetation and overhead branches.
• Keep both access routes clear of low-hanging branches and overgrown vegetation along their edges so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
